name: Number Ticker
hint: Press + Pledge or Studio order: the wheels carry right to left and blur with speed.
description: Animated number whose digits are physical wheels: pass `value` and each column springs on an endless 0–9 reel keyed by place value. In carry mode it travels the true distance like a mechanical counter (9 → 0 carries the next wheel), or it takes the shortest path. Columns start from the right like a carry, smear with a vertical motion blur proportional to their speed, new thousands separators and digits grow in, and compact units roll (999.9K → 1.0M). Up and down changes flash an arrow and a tint (inverted or neutral when up is bad). Formats via Intl, inherits any font size, announces the settled value once, cuts straight to the value under reduced motion. `demo` shows it on a live crowdfunding launch page.
intents: live fundraising total that ticks up
count up stat on scroll into view
stock price ticker with up down flash
usage: <NumberTicker value={n} format="currency" label="Raised so far" /> for any figure that changes in place: totals, prices, counts, KPIs. It inherits font size and weight, so the same component sits in a 13px table cell or a 96px hero. Format with `format` (integer, decimal, currency, compact, compact-currency, percent), `decimals`, `currency`, `locale`, or raw Intl.NumberFormat `options`; add units with `prefix` / `suffix`. Use carry mode for totals that only grow, `direction="shortest"` for values that wander (prices, rates); set `cueTone="inverted"` where up is bad (a cost) or `"neutral"`, or `cue={false}`. Give it a `label`; set `announce` on the one figure a screen reader should hear change (it speaks the settled value once). `Ticker` is the same component under its older name.

keyboard.does: Moves through + Pledge, + Studio order, Refund and Pause (or Resume); the number itself is not a stop.
Adds a pledge, adds a studio order, refunds one pledge, or pauses and resumes the live stream; the totals roll to their new values.

screenReader: The rolling digits are hidden from screen readers; a visually hidden copy reads `label` then the formatted value (with string `prefix` and `suffix`), or "loading". With `announce` that copy is a polite, atomic status region that speaks the settled value once, about 0.9s after it stops changing, never the frames in between; `announceEvery` spaces announcements further apart. The up/down cue is decoration and is not read.

dataProps.description: The number to show. Changing it rolls the wheels to the new value. null shows the loading placeholder.
How the number is formatted (percent expects a fraction: 0.42 → 42%).
Fraction digits. Defaults per format (decimal and currency 2, percent 1, compact 1 above 1,000). With the default "integer" format a value that has a fraction keeps up to two places; pass 0 to round.
ISO currency code for currency formats.
BCP 47 locale for separators and symbols (digits stay Latin). Default: the locale of the nearest <Theme> ("en-US" when none sets one).
Raw Intl options merged over the format's own, e.g. { style: "unit", unit: "kilometer" } or { signDisplay: "always" }.
Text before the number ("~", "Up to "). Strings are included in what screen readers hear.
Text after the number (" /mo", " users"). Sits right after the digits; the up/down arrow goes after it.

Flash an up / down arrow and tint beside the number when the value changes. Space for the arrow is kept at all times (about half a character), so nothing shifts; turn it off for a number set inside a sentence.
Which way the digits roll: carry, shortest, direct.
Colour of the up/down flash: default paints up green and down red; inverted paints up red (a cost, a latency); neutral uses the accent for both.
Which side the arrow sits on (start for right-aligned table cells).
With countUp, the number it counts up from when it scrolls into view.
What the number is ("Raised so far"). Read before the value by screen readers.
Speak changes in a polite live region: the settled value once (about 0.9s after it stops changing), never the frames in between.
Minimum ms between announcements, for values that change all the time (a live total).
Show a placeholder bar instead of the number.
Width of the loading placeholder in em.

Only with `demo`: font size of the board's hero total, sm 56px, md 84px, lg 104px; it still shrinks to fit a narrow board. A number sets it in px exactly. The ticker itself inherits its font size from its parent.
Show the launch-day board (live pledges, reward table) instead of a single number. Leave off in real UI. `live`, `interval` and `size` only apply to it.
The number's root span.
Any other attribute (id, aria-*, data-*) goes to the root <span>. className and style are merged with the component's own.
